paragraphs: Friend, this passage is heavy, and I'm not going to pretend it isn't. Judah prayed a real prayer. They said, "We acknowledge our wickedness, O LORD," and they asked Him to remember His covenant (Jeremiah 14:20-21). But the LORD says they have forsaken Him and turned their back, and that they "have not turned from their ways" (Jeremiah 15:6-7).

Here's the lesson I take from it. Words that sound right are not the same as a heart that turns. Judah said the right things in the middle of a drought, but the LORD looked at where they actually stood. I think that's a gentle warning for every one of us: don't just say sorry, turn.

And look at what keeps this from being only bad news. Judah's prayer got one thing exactly right: the rain comes from "the LORD our God" (Jeremiah 14:22), not from idols. That's where hope belongs, and it's where I put mine too, after those years in the back of a drawer. So today, baker, bring your whole self to Him, and let your turning be as real as your prayer. This one's not over, and I'll be right here with the ovens warm.
